statement: A Scottish invasion of England took place near Carlisle on 8 July 1648 as part of the Second English Civil War.
The First English Civil War between Royalist supporters of Charles I and an alliance of Parliamentarian and Scottish forces had ended in 1646.
Charles I was defeated in 1646.
Charles I was imprisoned in 1646.
Charles I continued to negotiate with several factions among his opponents.
Charles I's negotiations sparked the Second English Civil War in 1648.
The Second English Civil War began with a series of mutinies and Royalist uprisings in England and Wales.
A Scottish faction known as the Engagers supported Charles.
The Engagers raised an army.
The Engagers' army was under the command of James Hamilton, Duke of Hamilton.
The Engagers' army marched south to support the uprisings.
The Engagers' army crossed into England.
The Engagers' army combined with English Royalists under Marmaduke Langdale.
The combined army continued along the west coast road.
The combined army was some 24,000 strong.
Much smaller Parliamentarian forces were commanded by Major General John Lambert.
Major General John Lambert's forces fell back in front of the combined Royalist army.
Lieutenant General Oliver Cromwell concentrated 9,000 men in north Yorkshire on 12 August.
Cromwell's forces crossed the Pennines.
Cromwell's forces fell on the flank of the Royalist army at Preston on 17 August.
The Royalist army at Preston was much larger than Cromwell's forces.
Hamilton did not contemplate that Cromwell would act recklessly.
Hamilton was caught with his army on the march.
Hamilton's army had large detachments too far away to intervene.
A blocking force consisted of about 3,000 English Royalist infantry.
Many of the English Royalist infantry were ill-armed.
Many of the English Royalist infantry were inadequately trained.
The English Royalist blocking force proved no match for the Parliamentarians.
Most of the Parliamentarians were well-trained veterans from the New Model Army.
A ferocious hour-long fight took place.
These Royalists broke and fled after the fight.
A second round of prolonged infantry hand-to-hand fighting took place for control of a bridge over the River Ribble immediately south of Preston.
The Parliamentarians were victorious in the second round of fighting.
The Parliamentarians fought their way across the bridge as night fell.
Most of the survivors were to the south of Preston.
Nearly all of the survivors were Scottish.
Most of the survivors had not been engaged.
The survivors were still at least as strong as the whole Parliamentarian army.
The survivors fled towards Wigan in a night march.
The survivors were hotly pursued.
On 19 August, the survivors were hungry, cold, soaking wet, exhausted, and short of dry powder.
The survivors turned to fight at Winwick on 19 August.
More than three hours of furious but indecisive close-quarters fighting took place.
The Parliamentarians fell back after the fighting.
The Parliamentarians carried out a flank march.
The Scots routed when they saw the Parliamentarian force appear.
Parliamentarian cavalry pursued the Scots.
Parliamentarian cavalry killed many Scots.
All of the surviving Scots surrendered.
The Scottish infantry surrendered either at Winwick church or in Warrington.
The Scottish cavalry surrendered on 24 August at Uttoxeter.
Winwick was the final battle of the war.
Charles I was beheaded on 30 January 1649.
England became a republic on 19 May 1649.
